name: PA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+15 partisan lean gives Republicans almost no structural path
Scanlon's overwhelming fundraising edge: about $1.34 million raised versus $21,000 for Manganaro
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98 percent
No polls or expert ratings flag any vulnerability for the incumbent
model.rationale: The district's D+15 lean, Scanlon's roughly sixty-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing her near 98 percent all point the same direction, and no polling or ratings suggest the challenger has gained traction.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or any polling showing the race in single digits would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon (D) is running.

overview:
Pennsylvania's fifth district leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon returns after renomination with every structural advantage intact. The district's fifteen-point Democratic lean, combined with her incumbency, leaves Republicans little room in the general election. Scanlon has raised about $1.3 million and holds roughly $470,000 on hand, while challenger Nicholas Manganaro has raised about $21,000 with minimal cash remaining. Outside groups have spent modestly supporting her and almost nothing against her.

Prediction markets price her win near 98 percent, and no public polling or expert ratings flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects Scanlon to win by roughly twenty-three points, in line with the district's fundamentals. With no evidence of a competitive contest emerging, the seat is rated Safe Democratic with high confidence.
